# Anāhitā walks into a mythic name restoration firm

Somewhere right now, in a mythic name restoration office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Anāhitā**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Hymn to the Waters.** Aredvi Sura Anāhitā is praised as the mighty river that flows from Mount Hara into the sea Vourukaša, feeding the seven rivers of the earth.  The Yasht asks her to come down from the stars to receive sacrifice, and it promises her worshippers fertile fields, healthy children, victorious armies, and long life.  She is simultaneously a cosmic geography and a personal savior.

**Royal Patroness.** Artaxerxes II and later Achaemenid kings invoked Anāhitā in their inscriptions alongside Ahura Mazdā and Mithra.  Her cult spread through the empire, and temples were erected to her at Ecbatana, Susa, and Babylon.  For the Iranian aristocracy, devotion to Anāhitā was a marker of loyalty and legitimacy.

### Freshwater & Hydrology

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The macrons and acute restore the Avestan vowel length of the Iranian water-goddess.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Anāhitā was always going to be re-derived wherever fertility, water, wisdom matters.

### Yoga, Meditation & Holistic Wellness

## Not the First Rebrand

Anāhitā absorbed and was absorbed by neighboring goddesses.  In Armenia she was identified with the indigenous goddess Nana or Nanē, and with the Greek Artemis and Tyche. The office is only the latest translation.
